findings.text: assert pulse.id == f'{pulse.archive}:{pulse.name}' compares two strings the test itself supplied: id was passed as f'{archive.id}:{pulse_name}', archive and name were passed separately, and the generated model composes nothing, so the assertion holds whatever the code does. Reinstating the truncation defect in any reader would leave it green; only editing the test's own input reddens it, which is what the recorded 179e16f1 arm did.

The {archive}:{name} composite identity is stated in slot descriptions only: nothing validates id against archive and name, so a caller can write a Pulse whose id is a substring of its name and MERGE onto the short key the previous review flagged. The repair moved the collision guarantee into prose rather than into a guard.

archive_host_key re-declares the operator-exclusion host comparison already owned by scripts/codac_uda_prototype/reader.py:23, and the two disagree on IP addresses, where the prototype's key for 192.0.2.10 is the prefix 192 and this one compares addresses exactly. Two enforcement paths for one exclusion rule answer differently for the same host set.

The module docstring states that production readers share the host comparison through archive_host_key, but at the reviewed head no production module imports it, so the sentence asserts a caller that does not exist; a reader may treat endpoint policy as already enforced at connection time.
